question.:question/problem:
Find the specific solution to the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={e}^{-2(x - 4)-y}$ given that  $\,y(4)=2.$

$y(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡($
{{field-1}} $)$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We first find the general solution and then apply the given initial condition to find a particular solution.

Separating variables and integrating both sides with respect to $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & ={e}^{-2(x - 4)-y} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & ={e}^{-2(x - 4)}{e}^{-y} \\ {e}^{y}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & ={e}^{-2(x - 4)} \\ \int {e}^{y}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int {e}^{-2(x - 4)}\,\text{d}x \\ \int {e}^{y}\,\text{d}y & =\int {e}^{-2(x - 4)}\,\text{d}x \\ {e}^{y} & =-\frac{1}{2}{e}^{-2(x - 4)}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the natural logarithm to both sides, we find the general solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{y}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(-\frac{1}{2}{e}^{-2(x - 4)}+C) \\ y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(-\frac{1}{2}{e}^{-2(x - 4)}+C).\end{aligned}
$$

We now apply the condition $y(4)=2$ to find $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y(4) & =2 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(-\frac{1}{2}{e}^{0}+C) & =2 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(C-\frac{1}{2}) & =2 \\ C-\frac{1}{2} & ={e}^{2} \\ C & =\frac{2{e}^{2}+1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Thus the particular solution of $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={e}^{-2(x - 4)-y}$ that satisfies the condition $y(4)=2$ is

$$
y=\operatorname{ln}⁡\left(\frac{-{e}^{-2(x - 4)}+2{e}^{2}+1}{2}\right).
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the particular solution to the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{{y}^{2}}{{(x + 4)}^{2}}+{y}^{2}$ that satisfies $y(-5)=1.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We first find the general solution and then apply the given initial condition to find a particular solution.

Separating variables and integrating both sides with respect to $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{{y}^{2}}{{(x + 4)}^{2}}+{y}^{2} \\ \frac{1}{{y}^{2}}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{{(x + 4)}^{2}}+1 \\ \int \frac{1}{{y}^{2}}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{{(x + 4)}^{2}}+1)\,\text{d}x \\ \int \frac{1}{{y}^{2}}\text{d}y & =\int \frac{1}{{(x + 4)}^{2}}\,\text{d}x+\int \,\text{d}x \\ -\frac{1}{y} & =-\frac{1}{(x + 4)}+(x + 4)+C \\ \frac{1}{y} & =\frac{1-{(x + 4)}^{2}-C(x + 4)}{(x + 4)} \\ y & =\frac{(x + 4)}{1-{(x + 4)}^{2}-C(x + 4)}.\end{aligned}
$$

We conclude that the general solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{(x + 4)}{1-{(x + 4)}^{2}-C(x + 4)},\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an arbitrary constant. 

We now apply the initial condition $y(-5)=1$ to find $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y(-5) & =1 \\ \frac{-1}{1-(-1)^{2}-C(-1)} & =1 \\ \frac{-1}{C} & =1 \\ C & =-1\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus the particular solution of $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{{y}^{2}}{{(x + 4)}^{2}}+{y}^{2}$ that satisfies the condition $y(-5)=1$ is

$$
y=\frac{(x + 4)}{1+(x + 4)-{(x + 4)}^{2}}\,.
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the particular solution to the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+2(x + 3){e}^{-y}=3{(x + 3)}^{2}{e}^{-y}$ that satisfies $y(-2)=1.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We first find the general solution and then apply the given initial condition to find a particular solution.

Separating variables and integrating both sides with respect to $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+2(x + 3){e}^{-y} & =3{(x + 3)}^{2}{e}^{-y} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =3{(x + 3)}^{2}{e}^{-y}-2(x + 3){e}^{-y} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =(3{(x + 3)}^{2}-2(x + 3)){e}^{-y} \\ {e}^{y}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =3{(x + 3)}^{2}-2(x + 3) \\ \int {e}^{y}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (3{(x + 3)}^{2}-2(x + 3))\,\text{d}x \\ \int {e}^{y}\,\text{d}y & =\int (3{(x + 3)}^{2}-2(x + 3))\,\text{d}x \\ {e}^{y} & ={(x + 3)}^{3}-{(x + 3)}^{2}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the natural logarithm to both sides, we find the general solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{y}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({(x + 3)}^{3}-{(x + 3)}^{2}+C) \\ y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({(x + 3)}^{3}-{(x + 3)}^{2}+C)\end{aligned}
$$

We now apply the initial condition $y(-2)=1$ to find $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y(-2) & =1 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({1}^{3}-{1}^{2}+C) & =1 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡C & =1 \\ C & =e\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus the particular solution of $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+2(x + 3){e}^{-y}=3{(x + 3)}^{2}{e}^{-y}$ that satisfies the condition $y(-2)=1$ is

$$
y=\operatorname{ln}⁡({(x + 3)}^{3}-{(x + 3)}^{2}+e).
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the particular solution to the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{{y}^{2}}{{(x - 4)}^{2}}+{y}^{2}$ that satisfies $y(3)=1.$

$$

We conclude that the general solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{(x - 4)}{1-{(x - 4)}^{2}-C(x - 4)},\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}y(3) & =1 \\ \frac{-1}{1-(-1)^{2}-C(-1)} & =1 \\ \frac{-1}{C} & =1 \\ C & =-1\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus the particular solution of $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{{y}^{2}}{{(x - 4)}^{2}}+{y}^{2}$ that satisfies the condition $y(3)=1$ is
